result.title: Does Your Generalist Skill Optimizer Really Incentivize Agentic Tasks? Rethinking Skill Optimization via Bipartite Attribution
result.summary: Skill optimizers adapt an agent to long-horizon tasks, such as repairing a terminal environment, by rewriting its skill, a natural-language procedure in its context, and keeping the edits that raise success on a small dev set. On such tasks success is noisy, so a gain on a small dev set does not show that an edit helps, and a success score does not show what the edit costs. We introduce BiPA, which replays an optimizer's acceptance rule on candidates identical to its seed to measure what selection alone reports, and records each episode as a bipartite graph of turns and the text they read to trace extra input tokens to the behavior behind them. Across three optimizers, three agentic benchmarks and two models, the learned skills succeed about as often as their hand-written seed, 0.1 points higher on average. Their dev gains vanish on test: keeping the best of several candidates on at most 30 tasks reports gains this large even when none changed. They read about 16% more input tokens: the optimizers almost always add rules, half to re-check work and some to act one call at a time, and the agent follows them as extra turns, each re-sending the whole conversation. Four principles follow: accept an edit only if its gain exceeds what selection alone reports; charge it for the turns it adds, not for its length; let the editor delete and merge rules; show it what earlier rules cost. Code is available at https://github.com/valleysprings/BiPA.git.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 BiPA，通过重放优化器的接受规则并与同源候选对比、用「轮次—所读文本」二部图把额外输入 token 归因到具体行为，检验三种 skill optimizer 在 agentic 任务上的收益是否真实；结果显示学到的技能仅比手写种子高约 0.1 点，dev 增益在测试上消失，输入 token 增加约 16%。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「仅由选择产生的增益」对照和按新增轮次而非文本长度计费的成本归因，可能可供核查 latent 步骤或多轮 LOOK/THINK 的增益是否真实、以及贡献分配与实际成本评估，但对象是纯文本 agent 技能而非视觉 latent 推理，需进一步判断可迁移性。
